info.title: FastProof API
info.description: Test reporting server: projects, launches, uploads, results and attachments.

get.description: Replicas seen within a day with their test-management and analysis levels, and whether new data formats may be written (`FASTPROOF_TM_GATE`, `FASTPROOF_TM_GATE_SETTLE_SECONDS`; `analysis`: `FASTPROOF_ANALYSIS_GATE`, `FASTPROOF_ANALYSIS_GATE_SETTLE_SECONDS`). Needs `settings:write` without a project scope.

Health of the projects the caller can read (`launches:read` in each; at most 200, narrowed by `projects`): launches, pass rate of the results that ran, failures, unique errors first seen and regressed in the window, flaky tests and the median time to resolve. A project the caller cannot read never appears or counts. Needs ClickHouse (409 `clickhouse_required`).

post.description: Receives the webhook of a tracker with `sync: webhook` (no bearer token). The request must prove the secret named by `webhookSecretRef` (purpose `tracker-webhook`): GitHub `X-Hub-Signature-256` and Jira `X-Hub-Signature` (`sha256=` HMAC of the body), GitLab `X-Gitlab-Token`, Azure DevOps basic authentication with the secret as the password. A verified call only schedules a read of the issue it names through the tracker's API (at most one per issue per 5 seconds); its payload is never taken as the state; an issue that backs off after failed reads or is being read is left alone. Every refusal is the same `401` after the same minimum time. At most 120 calls per project and tracker per minute (`429`). Body at most 256 KiB.

parameters.description: the token of a media URL

200.description: the bytes, like the content route; no credentials needed

post.description: Queues a backtest of the project's decision history of the last `days` (1 to 730, default 180): every person's decision is replayed in time order against the memory folded from the decisions before it, with the live scoring, and the report gives the precision per band and the coverage (`GET .../analysis/backtest/latest`). Answers the task (202). A backtest replays for at most 10 minutes (the report is then `truncated`). 409 `analysis_disabled` while Analysis is off, 409 `upgrade_in_progress` while older replicas run, 409 `limit_reached` while a backtest of the project is queued or running, or with too many open tasks. Needs `settings:write`.

get.description: The newest backtest report of the project (404 without one). Needs `projects:read`.
What FastProof Analysis answers for the project: the instance and project switches, ClickHouse, `pg_trgm`, the analysis replica gate, the features and the data windows. Needs `projects:read`.

Exports the project's decision events (what the memory learned, one JSON `DecisionEvent` per line) for an offline backtest (`fastproof analysis backtest --events <file>`). The author is the first 16 hex digits of sha256 of a random secret of the project and the author (stable within the project, not testable without the server's database). A page holds at most `limit` events and 8 MiB; when more are left it carries the `after` of the next one in `x-fastproof-next-after`. 409 `analysis_disabled` while Analysis is off. Needs `settings:write`.

post.description: Imports the history of Allure reports as finished launches dated at their reports, joined to the tests live results use (the Allure `historyId` is the FastProof series key). Multipart fields: `history` (required: `history/history.json` of an Allure 2 report, or the Allure 3 history file, a JSON line per report) and, for `allure2`, `historyTrend`, `durationTrend`, `categoriesTrend` and `retryTrend`. Limits: `history.json` 32 MiB, an Allure 3 file 256 MiB (a line 32 MiB, 1000 reports), each trend file 4 MiB, 500 000 results, 200 000 tests in `history.json`. One import per project at a time; 20 per project per day. A second import of the same files adds nothing. Reports older than the project's retention window are left out. Needs `settings:write`.

post.description: Merges launches (CI shards, re-runs) into a new launch or into one of them (`into`). A test run in several of them becomes one result with more attempts (the latest is the result, mixed outcomes are flaky in the run); counters, transitions, flakiness, defects and the series statistics are recomputed (the analysis may finish shortly after the answer: `analysing`). The other launches are hidden (`mergedInto`) and refuse further writes with 409 `launch_merged`; they come back on undo, possible until `undoUntil` (`FASTPROOF_MERGE_UNDO_HOURS`), and are deleted afterwards (a merge with `final` keeps them a couple of minutes for writes on their way). Repeating the same merge returns it (200) and copies what reached the launches since. Launches to merge must be finished with no upload in progress (409 `launch_running`, `launch_busy`); the target may run, but a finished target takes the merge only from its creator or a caller with `cases:sync` (409 `launch_finished`). Also 409 `launch_merged`, `launch_manual`, `launch_plan`, `merge_mixed` (debug or branch differ), `launch_rolled_up`, `merge_busy` (another merge or undo of the project runs); 413 `merge_too_large` (attempts or log bytes). `dryRun` answers counts (status `preview`) without merging and without locks.

post.description: Pre-signed S3 PUT URLs for attachments of the launch. Content the project already stores is linked at once (`exists`, only for callers who may read the launch, and only for content still in use).
